title: Workforce Coordinator
text:
Email: workforce@alnwickdolphins.com
Do we have enough Officials? Do we have the right mix of skills in the volunteers? Do we have who we need to be able to host galas? Are our volunteers armed with all the infomation and support they need?
Answering all these questions and more falls to the role of the workforce coordinator. They hold a key position on the committee, since the club would not exist without a healthy supply of well prepared volunteers!



Retaining and recruiting new volunteers throughout all of the roles within the club (committee, coaches, team managers, poolside helpers, officials).
Co-ordinating volunteers to ensure adequate cover is provided during galas home and away.
Ensuring that volunteers have the appropriate qualifications to enable them to continue in their role.
Identifying the future needs of the club in respect of positions that may become vacant in the future.





Good and effective communications skills
Some knowledge of the gala pyramid to ensure cover is provided
Knowledge of the requirements by either the Club or Swim England to enable volunteers to be poolside.

Volunteer Training

Alnwick Dolphins typically covers 100% of the cost of this training, to ensure the path to becoming a volunteer is as frictionless as possible, given their importance to the club.

Welfare Officer

title: SwimMark Coordinator
text:
SwimMark Coordinator
This essential role involves being the key contact and lead volunteer who manages a swimming club’s SwimMark accreditation process with Swim England.
SwimMark is an accreditation system, renewed every 12 months, which recognises a club is operating in a safe and compliant way and has achieved the minimum standard of safe and effective practice.

title: Marshall
text:
Marshall
Marshalls are responsible for ‘herding’ swimmers on poolside during an event to ensure each swimmer is where they need to be to make sure the gala runs to schedule. It can be hectic, loud and fast-paced poolside, so Marshalls play a key role in bringing some order to the chaos! No prior experience or swimming knowledge is needed to be a gala marshall. You must, however have a basic DBS check and undertake an online child safeguarding course. You can sign up to marshall at one of our events by responding to the link you will be sent via email when a gala is set up on Swim Manager.
To find out more about becoming a Marshall, speak to the club’s Workforce Coordinator or the Club Secretary.

title: Welcome to the Alnwick Dolphins Volunteer Team!
text:
Thank you for volunteering with Alnwick Dolphins.
Our swimming club cannot run without people who are willing to give their time, skills and energy to support swimmers.
Some volunteers will be visible on poolside. Others will work behind the scenes. Some will volunteer every week; others may help at occasional competitions or events.
Every contribution matters.
You do not need to be an experienced swimmer to volunteer.
You do not need to know all the rules.
You do not need to have volunteered before.
What matters is that you are willing to learn, work as part of a team and put the welfare and development of our swimmers at the centre of what you do.
This manual explains how volunteering at Alnwick Dolphins works and provides practical guidance for volunteers.
It should be read alongside the club’s formal policies and procedures.


You can talk to your swimmer’s coach, or contact us at chair@alnwickdolphins.com. You will receive occasional emails from the club inviting you to sign up for sporadic volunteering opportunities - please do respond to these if you can!
When the club hosts its own events at Willowburn, its all hands on deck! There are lots of volunteering jobs needed to help an event run smoothly. Take a look at the Gala Roles section for some options. When home galas are added to Swim Manager, various Jobs will be available to sign up for via the portal - if you’re unsure, just speak to any member of the coaching squad or committee.
Read on to find out about each type of role.

title: Gala Roles
text:
For galas hosted by Alnwick Dolphins, we need a team of people willing to put time into helping organise and staff the event. On Swim Manager there is the facility to sign up to the different roles for a specific gala - there is no requirement to fulfill that role for more than one gala, or for all days of multi-day galas (but obvioulsy it is easier to manage an event if the volunteers are the same on all days).
You don’t need to be in any other named role to help with a home gala - sign up as you see fit!
The small (but crucial!) volunteer roles that are generally needed and change each time are:



Lead organiser

This person takes responsibility for ensuring the gala checklist is completed on time for their gala. They ensure each named and unnamed role is filled as needed, and often also perform the role of Runner on the day. Each gala has its own Lead Organiser, and the role benefits from strong organisational and timekeeping skills. The organisation of a gala starts months before, so the time needed to perform this role is more than some other.

Ticket sales

To be physically present on the day and manage selling spectator tickets.

Raffle stand

To be physically present on the day and manage the raffle of donated goods.

Medal table

Manage the medals to be presented on gala day, ensuring there are enough of each type and that each swimmer receives the correct medal.

Runners

Ensure information flows as needed between all officials, medal table staff and team managers as needed.

Announcer

Use the sound system to announce all the events and housekeeping info on the day.

Set-up staff

On the day of a gala (or the night before, dependent on timings) we need a small army of volunteers to help set up the timing equipment, chairs, signage, tables etc. We also then need to tidy it all away at the end! The Lead Organiser for a home gala will advise you of when the set up and tidying up will take place.
Typically, those people who are already volunteering in other roles also assist with this work, since they are going to be present on the day anyway. However, if you’d like to offer to help with this for any particular home gala, either sign up on Swim Manager, or contact the Competition Secretary. They can put you in touch with the gala’s lead organiser who can assist you to find a way to contribute.




Team Managers

To host galas, we also need a whole set of Officials of various types - these are really important roles that are essential for hosting our own galas, but they do require a bigger commitment from volunteers. Please have a look at the Officials page for more information.

Officials

title: Fundraising Coordinator
text:
Email: 
Raising funds to support our club is really crucial. The Fundraising Coordinator provides a central point of contact for fundraising queries and takes the lead on developing opportunities for accessing grants and funding. Funds raised go towards providing all the kit necessary to give our swimmers the best experience and support we can, travel and related expenses, and funding training for new officials.
Successful fundraising also means that we can control the fees charged to the swimmers, so that being an Alnwick Dolphin is available to as wide a group as possible.
This is an exciting and fundamental role. Impact on the club will be determined by your own motivations and enthusiasm. As well as your ability to source funding opportunities, it is an opportunity to impact the growth and development of your club.
No knolwedge of swimming is necessary.



Identifying new and ongoing sources of funding and sponsorship
Preparing funding bids in partnership with club committee members as appropriate
To establish and develop effective working relationships with key local funding providers

title: Committee Roles
text:
These roles are held continuously from one AGM until the next. They are proposed, seconded and elected by the committee at the AGM. The minimum tenure is therefore one year, except in exceptional circumstances.
The Chairperson, Treasurer and Secretary together constitute the “Executive Officers of the Club”. The committee must be made up of these three people, plus at least four other elected club members.
The Committee meets in person at least quarterly, in Alnwick. AGM’s are held in May or June annually.
We always welcome enthusiastic new recruits, and if you have some time to spare we can work with you to help you find a way to contribute. However, these roles also benefit from some continuity, and are often held for a number of years at a time.
Where relevant, Swim England provides guides to each of these roles, which you can find on their website, and are linked in each role page that follows.

title: Coaches
text:
Swimming coaches are possibly the most important people in the club. Through their expertise and enthusiasm, they get to know all the swimmers in their squads, advocating for each swimmer and helping them achieve their goals.
You don’t need to be a swimmer or have prior involvement in the sport to start your coaching journey. New coaches start out as Assistant Coaches, before progressing to a Coach position. They can also then progress to Senior Coach.
The coaches ensure they maintain their training to a high standard. They devote a lot of their own time every week to train our swimmers and coordinate a varied, interesting and challenging training schedule that allows everyone to be stretched and challenged.
Coaches are self-organised and punctual, and report to the head coach.
Training is available through Swim England. You can find further details here. Alnwick Dolphins typically covers the full cost of this training through its Institute of Swimming vouchers. Because of this, we expect a Coach to stay in the role for at least one year.
To find out more about becoming a coach, speak to the club’s Workforce Coordinator, Head Coach, or Club Secretary.

title: Chairperson
text:
Email: chair@alnwickdolphins.com
The club chair is the principal officer for the club and is elected by the club members.
The chair provides direction and leadership to the club, dealing with issues as and when they arise. They are the ‘face’ of the committee and are intimately involved in all aspects of club organisation. This is a pivotal and highly rewarding role whose success and impact on the club will be determined by your own ambitions and enthusiasms. As well as your ability to guide and engage others, it is an opportunity to take on a new challenge and influence the future direction of your club.
Day to day jobs include but are not limited to:

chairing meetings of the committee
deciding the direction of the club
setting the goals and vision of the club
ensuring the club meets its objectives and vision
oversee decisions made by the management and other club personnel
ensure the club operates within the relevant legal frameworks, including Swim England laws

This varied role can (and does!) require a wide range of skills, including good knowledge of the club and competitive swimming, skills in organisation, diplomacy, public speaking and more. The time committment is varied but can be considerable. Its a challenging role but a massively reqarding one.

Alnwick Dolphins is a competitive amateur club. We attend a whole range of competitions across the region, and host our own fixtures at Willowburn pool. The competition secretary is responsible for maintaining the competition calendar.
The competition secretary gathers the relevant information, when available, for away events and adds them to Swim Manager, which is the platform that allows swimmers to enter events and pay their fees. Foster a positive, safe, and inclusive team culture aligned with club philosophy
Work alongside the club committee and chair to help shape the club’s long-term strategy and performance targets

Email: membership@alnwickdolphins.com
The Club Membership Secretary is the key link between the Club and the Swim England membership team. They ensure all club members are members of Swim England.
This role is the main point of contact for all club membership enquiries. They also Manage the club’s annual subscription and membership renewal process, ensuring membership fees are paid on time.

title: Officials
text:
Officials
A British Swimming Official is a voluntary role. To become an Official, you do not need any prior experience, or swimming knowledge. We always need to have new Officials coming through because swims cannot be recorded with Swim England if the right number of each type of Official is not present at our events. If swims cannot be recorded with Swim England, the swimmers’ times cannot be used to enter certain competitions.
Each of the following Official roles require a volunteer to commit to undertake (and keep up to date) relevant training and certification. They are listed in order of completion, so you must become a Timekeeper before you can become a Level 1 judge, for example. Which events they volunteer to help at is, however, up to them.
Being a registered Official does not mean you need to be available for every event! The more Officials we have, the less each will need to do to cover our home galas.

Timekeepers This is the entry level of roles for swimming officials. It requires you to complete a short course of official training and be at least 14 years old.
Judges Judges are people who have completed the Institute of Swimming training within a time limit of 11 months to receive their judging license (valid for 4 years).

There are thee levels of judges.
Level 1 is the lowest (entry) level judge. These judges can act as turn judges.
Level 2 judges require to have completed over 20 hours of level 1 judging duties alongside completing additional training. They must be over 15. Level 2 judges can be stroke judges.
Level 2S (Starter) is the highest judge level. This is for volunteers who have progressed through levels 1 and 2 and wish to qualify as an official Starter. They need to have completed at least 20 hours of Level 2 judging and additional training.

Starters Once a Level 2 judge has completed a minimum of 20 hours of post qualification experience they are eligible to undertake training to become an official Starter.
Referee A qualified individual (at least 20 years old) who has passed through the training pathway from basic timekeeper to judge to referee. Experience, training and mentoring are required to become a referee. You also need to pass an examination to qualify. If interested in finding out more, see Aquatics GB or speak to a member of the Committee.

title: Team Manager
text:
Team Manager
We need volunteers to act as team managers for both home and away galas. The Team Manager can be thought of as acting like a teacher taking their class on a school trip. Team Managers are responsible for ensuring that teams reach competitions safely and that athletes are cared for whilst at events.
They ensure that all swimmers are present and correct, get to where they need to be during the event, and act as a point of contact for parents/carers to ensure everybody has all relevant gala information. They play a crucial role in looking after all swimmers, and they take a lead on creating away gala itineraries, organising travel and timings, team kit etc. They should be a person capable of being calm under pressure and maintaining a positive team spirit which ensures our club is viewed positively wherever we go!
Often, the same people volunteer repeatedly to act as team managers, but it is important that we bring in new volunteers to the role, since if we cannot supply a team manager, our swimmers cannot attend away galas.
You will need an up to date DBS check, but no prior experience.
Training is available through two modules provided by Swim England and run regionally. You can find further details here. Alnwick Dolphins typically covers the full cost of this training through its Institute of Swimming vouchers. Because of this, we expect a Team Manager to stay in the role for at least one year.
To find out more about becoming a team manager, speak to the club’s Workforce Coordinator or the Club Secretary.

title: Welfare Officer
text:
Email: welfare@alnwickdolphins.com
This role is essential in providing a first point of contact for children, parents and adults within the club who have a safeguarding or welfare concern. This person is the advocate for the swimmers, and consequently stays somewhat appart from the Committee and other long term roles. Their responsibility is to act independently and in the best interests of an athlete at the club, putting their needs above that of others and the club itself.
The Welfare Officer has the right to attend Committee meetings but does not have the power to vote.



Ensure the club implements Wavepower, Swim England’s safeguarding policy and procedures correctly.
Be the first point of contact for all staff, volunteers, swimmers and their parents/carers for any issues concerning welfare, poor practice or potential or alleged abuse.
To ensure that all incidents are reported correctly and referred, in accordance with Wavepower.
Ensuring relevant roles have up to date DBS checks and safeguarding training.





Current DBS certification
Training: A.S.A Child Safeguarding courses.
